Bhilwara: A chemist in Rajasthan's Bhilwara is facing culpable homicide charges after a 17-year-old girl allegedly died following an injection administered by him at a local medical shop.

The incident reportedly occurred on November 11, when the girl was taken to the shop for treatment of fever. Her condition allegedly deteriorated after the injection, following which she was shifted to hospitals in Bhilwara and Udaipur for treatment.

The deceased, identified as Prachi, daughter of Rakesh Mehta, had reportedly been suffering from fever for several days. Her family initially took her to a medical shop in the Subhash Nagar police station area, where the chemist allegedly administered an injection without proper medical assessment.

According to local residents, the chemist had allegedly acted as a doctor and administered the injection to the girl.

Following the incident, Prachi was taken to a private medical facility in Bhilwara. As her condition worsened, she was referred to a private hospital in Udaipur, where she continued to receive treatment. However, she died on Saturday morning.

The girl's death triggered anger among local residents, who allegedly attempted to vandalise the medical shop and set it on fire. Police personnel reached the spot and brought the situation under control.

Subhash Nagar Police Station in-charge Kailash Kumar Bishnoi confirmed that the medical shop had been sealed following the incident. Police teams have also been constituted to trace and arrest the accused chemist.

The Times of India reports that a case has been registered against chemist Ramprasad Sharma under sections related to culpable homicide. Separate police teams have been deployed to locate and apprehend him.

Bishnoi further stated that a medical board conducted the post-mortem examination at the Udaipur hospital on Saturday evening. After the procedure, the girl's body was handed over to her family.
